request: The bakery app needs high-quality UX for ordering. It belongs under Feature #40 (Online ordering).

exchanges.say: You want ordering to feel high quality. Today the /order flow is five screens (flow:/order), the review screen where people pay has no error state (gap:error:/order) though it records payment_declined, and the screens already share Stepper, Button, and 14 design tokens. Three questions, riskiest first.

questions.ask: Which task has to feel high quality first: a first order for pickup, or something else? And how does the customer know it worked?
questions.default: A first order for pickup that ends on a confirmation with an order number, because one well-defined task is buildable and testable in one story.

questions.ask: Your order flow is five screens (/order, options, pickup, details, review). That feels long for a loaf of bread. Aim for three?
questions.default: Three screens, because the options and pickup screens only confirm a choice.

questions.ask: The pay screen has no error state today, though it already records payment_declined. When a payment fails, should the basket stay and a retry appear on the same screen?
questions.default: Keep the basket and offer a retry on the same screen.

answers.text: A customer picks bread, chooses a pickup time, and pays by card on the review screen as they do today, and knows the order went through: they see an order number and the pickup time.
Five screens is too many. Three screens at most: choose items, then pickup time and details together, then review and pay.
When a payment fails, keep the basket and show a message with a Try again button on the same screen.

exchanges.say: So: a first order for pickup, three screens at most, and a failed payment keeps the basket with a Try again button. A few more, including where the confirmation goes.

questions.ask: What does a customer need to see before paying to trust the order: the total, the pickup time, both?
questions.default: The total and the pickup time on the review screen, because surprise costs are the main reason people abandon an order.

questions.ask: Where does the confirmation with the order number go: its own screen after paying, or on the review screen once payment succeeds? Does it count toward the three?
questions.default: Its own screen after paying, not counted, because the three screens are the ones the customer works through.

questions.ask: Your config says web only. Check every screen at a phone width (390 px) and a desktop width (1280 px)?
questions.default: 390 px and 1280 px, the widths the web floors capture.

questions.ask: You have 14 design tokens and Button, Stepper, and BasketSummary components. Must the new flow use only those?
questions.default: Only existing tokens and components, counted over the changed files, because a new look is a design decision, not a story detail.

questions.ask: Is there wording that must appear exactly, such as the confirmation or the payment error message?
questions.default: Leave exact wording to you; the criteria name the elements, not the copy.

answers.text: Show the total price and the pickup time on the review screen before they pay.
The confirmation is its own screen after paying; it does not count toward the three.
Only our existing tokens and components; nothing new-looking.
I'm not sure about the wording yet. Leave it open and I'll write it with the shop staff.

exchanges.say: Nearly there: the confirmation is its own screen after paying. Two last ones: the pickup slots in #14, and one idea of mine you can say no to.

questions.ask: Open story #14 defines the pickup slots on /order/pickup, which moves onto the combined screen. Depend on #14 and reuse its slots?
questions.default: Depend on #14, so the slots are built once.

questions.ask: An idea while we're here: a loyalty stamp card on the confirmation screen, every tenth loaf free. Worth adding?

answers.text: Yes, depend on #14 and use its pickup slots on the combined screen.
That is not part of what I asked for; park it.

exchanges.say: Here is what done looks like: a customer goes from an empty basket to a paid order in at most 3 screens, then sees a confirmation screen with an order number and the pickup time; the review screen shows the total and the pickup time before they pay; a declined payment keeps the 2 basket items and shows a Try again button on the same screen; every screen fits at 390 px and 1280 px without horizontal scrolling; and the screens use only the existing tokens and components. It depends on #14 for the pickup slots. The wording is deferred to you and the shop staff, offline is deferred, and the loyalty stamp card is parked.
